 Hon'Ble Saurabh Lavania, J.

1. Sri Satish Chandra Verma, Advocate has filed Vakalatnama on behalf of opposite party No. 2 in
the Court today, which is taken on record.

2. Heard learned counsel for parties and perused the record.
3.

The present application has been filed for the following main relief(s):- "Wherefore it is most respectfully prayed that Hon;ble this court kindly be partly quash the impugned Chargsheet along with cognigence dated 17/09/2020 passed by A.C.J.M-3 Court No 27 Lucknow arising out of Case Crime No 395/2019 of police station -Saadatganj, District- Lucknow of Criminal case no.-
408/2020, U/S 498A, 323, 506 I.P.C and 3/4 D.P.Act (State Vs. Faiz Abbas & Other's) on the basis of compromise pending before Judicial Magistrate (A.T.S) Lucknow in the interest of justice.

It is further prayed that Hon'ble this court kindly be stayed the further proceeding in Criminal case No.- 408/2020, U/S 498A, 323, 506 I.P.C and 3/4 D.P.Act (State Vs. Faiz Abbas & Other's) pending in Judicial Magistrate (a.t.s.) Lucknow during pendency of this petition in the interest of justice.

It is further prayed that Hon;ble this court kindly be quash the entire proceeding of case no 408/2020 under section 498A, 323, 506 I.P.C and 3/4 D.P.Act arising out of case crime No-395/2019 police station -Saadatganj, District- Lucknow (State Vs.Faiz Abbas & Other's) pending before court Judicial Magistrate (A.T.S.) Lucknow in the interest of justice."
4.

It appears that after considering the averments made in the Application U/S 482 Cr.P.C. No.
11437 of 2023 and the documents in support thereof as also the submissions made by the learned counsel for the applicants, this Court vide order dated 22.11.2023 referred the matter to the concerned court for the purpose of verification of the compromise entered into between the parties.

5. It appears from the order dated 30.11.2023 (Annexure No.6) that the trial court has verified the compromise mentioning therein that the parties were present and they have admitted that they have entered into an agreement voluntarily and their signatures have been verified by their respective counsels before the court.

Principal Secretary and others (2014) 2 SCC 532 and Supreme Court Bar Association Vs. Union of India (1998) 4 SCC 409, according to which, in given facts, based upon the settlements between the parties the criminal proceedings can be quashed, as also the nature of dispute/crime, which is essentially matrimonial in nature, this Court is of the view that the present application is liable to be allowed as chances of ultimate conviction are extremely bleak and hence no useful purpose would be served by allowing the criminal proceedings to continue.
